transcript.text:
I can help with that. 'Oven won't come on' usually points to one of three things: a simple setting issue, a loss of power, or an internal fault. The most common cause is actually a setting rather than a breakage. If there was a recent power cut or the oven was switched off at the wall, the clock often resets into 'AUTO' mode. In this state, the oven will not heat until you switch it to MANUAL (often shown as a hand symbol) and set the correct time. To narrow this down quickly:
1. Is there any light on the display/clock face right now? Or is it completely dark?
2. If there is a display, is the clock flashing or showing 'AUTO' / 'A'? Please let me know what you see.
display is lit and flashing 0.00 with a little symbol. power went off for an hour last night

That flashing 0.00 after a power cut is probably the clock resetting into AUTO (automatic) mode. 1. Press the button with a 'hand' symbol (or sometimes labelled 'Manual') or press the 'Clock/Time' button repeatedly until the flashing stops and you can set the time.
2. Set the correct current time.
3. Try turning the oven on to a standard function (like Fan Oven). If it heats up after doing this, there is no fault – it was just in automatic mode. If it still does not heat once the clock is set correctly and you are in MANUAL mode, then we need to look at other causes.
ok set the time and it came on and heated. thanks

That is good news. It was just the clock resetting to 'Auto' mode after the power cut. One quick tip for next time: once you have set the time and it works, make sure you leave it in Manual (often a hand symbol) rather than switching the oven off at the wall socket. Switching it off at the wall will reset the clock back to Auto again, which can be confusing if you aren't expecting it. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

candidates: Clock/programmer set to AUTO after power interruption (high)
No mains supply (isolator, fuse, or cooker switch) (medium)
plan: The fault they reported is: "won't come on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
